summary: Satoru Fujiwara works in Buddhist studies. He was a researcher at the Shinshu Otani-ha Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and a lecturer at Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).

Satoru Harada is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Tokyo (~1971–1973), was a research member at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), and served as a professor at Kokushikan University (~2007–2017).

Satoru Noriyama studied Buddhist studies under Esho Mikogami. He served as a part-time lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and at Ryukoku University (attested 2003), later becoming a lecturer there (attested 2013).
Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned degrees including a doctorate from Bukkyo University and studied at the University of Michigan, being taught by Takao Kagawa, Luis O. Gómez, and others. He became president of Kyoto Bunkyo University in 2014.
Satoshi Ito is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University (~1980–1989) and became a professor at Ibaraki University (~2003).
Satoshi Kono specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature from the University of Tokyo and became a professor at Kogakkan University in 2000.

Satoshi Naiki works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned a PhD from Kyoto University, where he served as an assistant professor at the Center for Cultural Heritage Studies (attested 2016–2020).

Satya Narayan Goenka worked in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Sayagyi U Ba Khin (~1955–1969), taught students such as Joseph Goldstein and Stephen Batchelor, and founded the Vipassana Research Institute in 1985.

Satya Vrat Shastri was an Indologist and linguist who earned a PhD at Banaras Hindu University. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Delhi (1970–1995) and Vice-Chancellor of Shri Jagannath Sanskrit Vishvavidyalaya (~1989–1991).

Satyendra Nath Bose studied at Presidency University and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture. He taught at the University of Dhaka (1921–1945), served as Professor of Physics at the University of Calcutta (1945), and was Vice-chancellor of Visva-Bharati University (~1956–1958).

Sayadaw U Pandita was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mahasi Sayadaw and Nandasiri Sayadaw. He succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991) and served as abbot of the Paṇḍitārāma Meditation Center, which he founded.

Sayadaw U Sīlānanda studied at the University of Colombo and under Mahasi Sayadaw. He served as abbot of Mahavijjodaya Chaung Monastery (1960), founder-abbot of Dhammānanda Vihara (~1993–2005), and chancellor of the International Theravāda Buddhist Missionary University (1999).

Sayadaw U Thittila studied under Ashin Adiccavamsa and at Visva-Bharati University (~1933–1934). He served as librarian for the Buddhist Society (~1938–1944) and became a lecturer in Buddhist philosophy at the University of Rangoon in 1952.

Sayagyi U Ba Khin was a Buddhist and religious studies teacher who studied under Saya Thetgyi (~1937–1945). He founded the International Meditation Centre and taught students including Satya Narayan Goenka, Ruth Denison, and Mother Sayamagyi.
Sayaka Sonoda specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at Toyo University under the supervision of Shinobu Yamaguchi.
Sayori Tsubota specializes in Indology. She was a PhD student at Osaka University (attested 2020) and became a JSPS postdoctoral fellow at Tohoku University (attested 2026).

Scott A. Mitchell works in Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the Graduate Theological Union under Richard K. Payne (attested 2008), served as professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies, and held presidential posts at Numata Center (attested 2026).

Scott Pacey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his doctorate from the Australian National University in 2011 and served as a lecturer in Buddhist thought and practice at the University of Manchester (attested 2014).
Sean D. Gaffney specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski (attested 2003) and also held a post there (attested 1996).
